ground.purpose: The page and every section; the header when solid; the intro.

raised.purpose: One tonal step up: specimen tiles, the lens interior, the limits panel.

line.purpose: Text color at 8%: row dividers and resting inset rings.

line-2.purpose: Text color at 15%: control rings, list tops, ruler minor ticks.

text.purpose: Headings, body, figures, icon array dots.

text-2.purpose: Leads, descriptions, nav at rest, scan tags.

muted.purpose: Metadata, hints, unfilled states; 5.6:1 on ground.

lime.purpose: The one color that acts or is live: actions, focus, selection, scan line, ruler mark, current step, lead evidence figure.

teal.purpose: Scan material: lit speckle, cross-sections, specimen tint, 17-number bars, ASCII footer.

teal-deep.purpose: Dark end of the scan material; no-WebGL fallback band.

amber.purpose: The reflective skin surface line in the scan. Scan material only.

att-4.purpose: Attention ramp stop 4; shares the lime value on purpose.

urgent.purpose: Refer urgently, its leading score fill, form errors, failed send. Always with its words.

review.purpose: Refer for review, its leading score fill, the probably-sent state. Always with its words.

routine.purpose: Routine follow-up and the sent confirmation. Always with its words.

display.purpose: Hero headline only. clamp(40px, 11.4vw, 56px) at line height 1 on phones.

display-statement.purpose: The privacy statement; words come into focus with scroll.

numeral.purpose: Evidence counts; the denominator in muted grey.

headline.purpose: Section headings; clamp(34px, 3vw, 46px) inside the pinned case scene.

figure.purpose: Metric values. Siblings: team names clamp(36px, 3.6vw, 52px), facts and score values 32px (26px pinned).

verdict.purpose: The triage suggestion, in its triage color.

title.purpose: Step titles, panel and FAQ headings.

lead.purpose: Paragraph under a heading, secondary grey, max about 34em.

body.purpose: Running text; tabular figures are on page-wide.

nav.purpose: Header links; field labels use the same size at 500.

small.purpose: Metadata, legends, help text in muted grey.

annotation.purpose: Scan tags, ruler readout, band notes; 13px for the cutoff note and keycaps.

wordmark.purpose: Lowercase "nevio" beside the mark; the only 600 weight.

narrative.overview:
The page is an instrument, not a brochure. Everything sits on one scan-black ground, and the only light in the room is the visitor's pointer: where it moves, a faint speckle field lights up in teal; in the hero, an illustrated cross-section of skin is acquired left of a lime scan line that follows it. Below the fold the light stops being illustration and becomes evidence. Real biopsy-confirmed specimens are shown first as the research model sees them, its own feature maps on the attention ramp, and develop into the photo where the pointer looks. Scrolling reads as depth: a millimetre ruler at the left edge goes from the surface down to 2 mm.

Density is low and deliberate. Big Host Grotesk headlines with tight tracking, a lead paragraph, then one instrument per section: the specimen grid, the case lens and its readout, the phone, the icon arrays, the statement over the device edge, the form. Sections are separated by space and hairlines, never by a change of ground. Color is rationed by role: lime acts, teal and amber are scan material, the attention ramp is the model's, and the triage colors speak only when a result does.

The world refuses two things by name: the medical template (white ground, clinical blue, stock clinicians) and the generic AI page (purple glow, rows of equal cards). Light here is always caused by something, the pointer or the model, and nothing moves on its own after the intro.
keyCharacteristics: One scan-black ground on every section; depth from light, tonal steps and hairlines, not from shadows or glows.
The pointer is the light: the WebGL scan layer is still until the pointer lights it.
Real model internals as imagery: 12 x 12 feature maps on a six-stop attention ramp, cropped and scaled exactly like the photo they sit on.
Lime is the one color that acts; triage colors appear only with their words.
Host Grotesk alone, 400 and 500, tight display tracking, tabular figures everywhere.
6 px control corners, 4 px tags and tiles, circles only for lenses and dots.
One authored motion moment (the intro and the hero sweep); everything after that answers the pointer, the scroll or a new value.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: Lime marks what acts or what is live right now. It is never a second brand color, never a large fill, and never emphasis on static text.

rules.name: The Words Attached Rule
rules.body: Urgent, review and routine appear only where a result or a status is stated, always beside the words that name it. Only the leading score's fill takes the verdict's color; the others stay neutral.

rules.name: The Same Ground Rule
rules.body: Every section sits on scan-black. The cross-section bands are light drawn on that ground, not colored panels.

rules.name: The Mirror Rule
rules.body: The :root tokens are normative, but the WebGL shader, the attention ramp array, the specimen scan LUT, the ASCII footer and the inline logo marks carry literal copies of these values. Change a token and its copies together.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Host Grotesk only. Hierarchy comes from size, weight (400 against 500) and tracking, never from a second face, italics or all caps.

rules.name: The Tight at Scale Rule
rules.body: Tracking tightens as size grows: -0.015em at 22 px, -0.03em around 32 to 40 px, -0.035 to -0.04em at headline and display sizes. Body text is never tracked.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Every heading, label, button and tag is in sentence case with no period on headings, no eyebrow above a heading, and no arrow after a link.

rules.name: The Asymmetric Pair Rule
rules.body: A heading or text column paired with an instrument is asymmetric (5 : 6, 6 : 5 or 7 : 5). Equal columns are only for like items compared side by side (the two evidence grids, the three privacy facts, the team, the specimens), and they are never boxed cards.

rules.name: The Light Is Depth Rule
rules.body: Things come forward because they are lit, not because they cast shadows. No colored shadow, no glow, no text shadow; drop shadows are black and only under the phone, the form card and the toast.

rules.name: The 6 px Rule
rules.body: Every pressable thing has 6 px corners. No pills, no cut corners, nothing above 10 px except the phone's physical body.

dos: **Do** keep every section on scan-black (#05080A) and separate sections with section padding (clamp 120 to 176 px) and hairlines.
**Do** reserve lime for what acts or is live: buttons, focus, selection, link hover, the scan line, the ruler mark, the current step, given ticks, changed cells and the lead evidence figure.
**Do** put urgent, review and routine only beside the words they stand for, and give the verdict a shape that differs by tone (solid dot, half-filled ring).
**Do** draw edges as 1 px inset rings at 8% or 15% of the text color, and use raised black (#0A1013) for wells and panels.
**Do** label any drawn scan that is not data as an illustration, and say plainly when a layer is computed by the research model.
**Do** crop and scale each model map exactly like the photo under it, normalized per photo, and recompute the maps if the model changes.
**Do** set everything in Host Grotesk at 400 and 500 (600 only for the wordmark), sentence case, tabular figures, tightening tracking as size grows.
**Do** keep the scan still until the pointer lights it, and redraw only on pointer, scroll and resize.
**Do** give every motion a reason (acquire, develop, rescore, settle) and a reduced-motion state that shows the final frame.
**Do** keep pressable targets at least 44 px tall on touch layouts, and keep muted text at or above 4.5:1 on the surface it sits on.
donts: **Don't** use violet, lavender, indigo or purple anywhere in the system; real photos keep their own color.
**Don't** change a section's background color or add colored bands; the cross-sections are light drawn on the same ground.
**Don't** set labels in all caps or letterspaced caps, and don't put eyebrow labels over headings.
**Don't** use italics or any monospace face; the ASCII footer draws Host Grotesk characters on a grid.
**Don't** add glows as decoration: no colored box-shadow halos, text shadows, neon outlines or blurred color blobs. Light appears only where the pointer is or where the model responds.
**Don't** use lime as a second brand color, a large fill, or emphasis on static text such as role labels or bullets.
**Don't** use teal, amber or the attention ramp for UI chrome; they are scan material and model data.
**Don't** let anything move on its own after the intro: no loops, drifting backgrounds, autoplay or pulsing elements (the spinner while the form sends is the one exception).
**Don't** round controls into pills, cut corners, or use hard offset shadows; nothing above 10 px except the phone's physical body.
**Don't** put a lesion photo in the first viewport; the hero shows only the illustrated cross-section.
**Don't** build rows of boxed, equal cards or a white, clinical-blue medical template look.
